summary: A national, cleaned CSV of all US-licensed wineries, distilleries, and FAA-permitted importers/wholesalers sourced directly from the TTB's weekly-updated public permittee download — approximately 20,000–25,000 records covering ~11,450 wineries and ~3,081 distilleries. Important caveat: brewery registrations are classified as tax return information under IRC Section 6103 and are NOT included in TTB's public list, so the product is accurately scoped as a winery + distillery directory. Target buyers are hop suppliers, packaging vendors, equipment companies, POS platforms (Toast, Arryved), beverage distributors, compliance consultants, and B2B SaaS companies selling into the craft beverage industry — audiences currently paying $179–$2,400/year for similar niche databases.

audience.who: B2B vendors selling into the craft beverage industry: equipment suppliers, ingredient/hop companies, POS platforms (Toast, Arryved), insurance providers (craft beverage liability), compliance/permitting consultants, barrel brokers, packaging companies, marketing agencies, and SaaS tools targeting wineries and distilleries. These buyers need accurate premise addresses and operating names to cold-outreach or direct-mail new and established permit holders. The 'new permit flag' in the TTB data also creates a high-value new-opener segment for early-stage vendor outreach.

data_wanted: TTB FAA Permittee List — publicly downloadable CSV/JSON from https://www.ttb.gov/public-information/foia/list-of-permittees with no authentication required. Published weekly. Confirmed permit types available: Wine Producers & Blenders (direct CSV: https://www.ttb.gov/system/files/2025-04/FRL_Wine_Producer_and_Blender_Permit_List.csv), Distilled Spirits Plants (DSP), Basic Permit Importers, Basic Permit Wholesalers. Fields per record: Permit_Number, Owner_Name, Operating_Name (trade/DBA name), Street, City, Prem_Zip, Prem_County, New_Permit_Flag. NOTE: Brewery/brewer registrations are explicitly excluded per IRC Section 6103 — the title of this product must be scoped to wineries, distilleries, importers, and wholesalers only.

evidence.source: TTB official List of Permittees page — confirms public CSV/JSON downloads by permit type, updated weekly, no auth required
evidence.quote: TTB provides the entire list of currently publicly available permittees in JSON format, with downloadable CSV files based on industry member type, with updates posted weekly.

evidence.source: WIN Data (wineindustrydata.com) — paid subscription product selling winery contact database with job-role-level exports to CSV/MailChimp
evidence.quote: Professional subscription costs $2,400 annually for full database access and export functionality — exportable by job type including Owner, Principal, Winemaker, Tasting Room, Wine Club, Finance.

evidence.source: Vinaty wine company database — 22,549 wine company contacts from 169 countries, sold at €179–€395 per access tier
evidence.quote: Essential tier €179 for 1,250 company views (3 months); Maximum tier €395 for 5,000 company views (12 months) — includes phone/email downloads and weekly updates.

evidence.source: Apify TTB Alcohol Permittee Scraper — third-party paid scraper built on top of the same public TTB data, confirming commercial demand
evidence.quote: Scrapes winery, distillery, importer and wholesaler permit lists with owner names, operating names, locations and new permit flags. Gold tier: $2.50 per 1,000 records — pay-per-result pricing.

evidence.source: WineAmerica / WineEconomist — US winery count confirming scale of the addressable database
evidence.quote: Total number of wineries in the US: 11,450 (2025). Combined with ~3,081 distilleries and importers/wholesalers, the cleaned dataset represents 20,000+ B2B records.

willingness_to_pay.signal: Competitors charge $179–$2,400/year for subsets of this same audience: WIN Data asks $2,400/yr for US winery contacts alone; Vinaty charges up to €395 for 5,000 international wine company views; Apify's TTB scraper charges $2.50–$3.50 per 1,000 records on a pay-per-use basis. B2B equipment suppliers, POS platforms, and ingredient vendors all need fresh permit-holder lists for outreach — the 'new permit flag' creates an especially valuable new-opener segment since these businesses are actively buying their first equipment, POS systems, and ingredients. A one-time download at $49–$79 is a clear no-brainer compared to a $2,400/yr subscription.

first_sale_path.channel: Gumroad one-time download ($49 standard, $79 with new-opener segment highlighted). Post in: r/winemaking, r/homebrewing (note: hobbyist but also has industry), r/smallbusiness, LinkedIn groups 'Craft Beverage Professionals', 'Wine Industry Network', 'Distilled Spirits Industry'. Cold outreach angle: email hop suppliers, packaging vendors, and compliance consultants directly using the Brewers Association supplier directory as a starting point.
first_sale_path.angle: Title: 'US Winery & Distillery Directory 2026 — 20,000+ Licensed Producers (TTB Public Data, CSV)'. Key selling points: (1) Direct from the federal permit authority — TTB data, not web-scraped guesses; (2) Includes new permit flag to identify recently licensed openers; (3) Clean CSV with name, DBA, full address, county, permit type — ready for mail merge or CRM import; (4) Updated from weekly TTB source; (5) Fraction of the cost of WIN Data ($2,400/yr) or Vinaty (€395). Distinct because it covers ALL permit types (winery + DSP + importer + wholesaler) in a single file, scoped to the US, sourced from a government authority.
